The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-14T12:27:19Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-14T12:27:45Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told or took part. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-14T12:21:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-14T12:29:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 8 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 33 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-14T12:30:13Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 29.3% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 28.4% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9416666666666667% {series_before} before it began, 29.3125% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-14T12:27:40Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-14T12:27:55Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-14T12:27:55Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-14T12:28:00Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 12:27:19 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-14T12:28:04Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-14T12:28:05Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 12:21 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-14T12:28:05Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-14T12:28:07Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 14 12:22 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-14T12:28:07Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-14T12:28:08Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-14T12:28:08Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 19 {T11.3} seconds before 12:27:19 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-14T12:28:08Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 124 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-14T12:28:10Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-14T12:28:10Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-14T12:28:10Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 2 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 12:28:10 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-14T12:28:13Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-14T12:28:14Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-14T12:28:21Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-14T12:28:28Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 12:29 {T19.2} - up to 158s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-14T12:30:13Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 12:28 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-14T12:30:13Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-14T12:30:13Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [monthly-spend-feature] OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-14T12:31:50Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/581

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-14T12:21:31Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - [P2] 2026-11-14T12:27:18Z {P2.1} flag-toggle an-unrelated-feature by admin: feature flag an-unrelated-feature was switched on - found only by Argus's read of the flag provider's history: it came after 2026-11-14T12:22:00Z {P2.2}, where the investigation's reads of the changes ended
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 11:51–12:20 {G7e5d.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 30 {G46bc.2} minutes, 11:51–12:20 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 11:51–12:27 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 40.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 12:24 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 26 {Gad41.2} minutes, 11:52–12:17 {Gad41.3}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 {G971b.1} / on 99 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 12:21 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 12:21–12:27 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 12:22–12:27 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-14T12:21:31Z {C1.1}. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to 20-40% {C1.3}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py returns `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`, where `bought_this_month` is the purchases flagged `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list there, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError. That is not an edge case. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, `render_spend_summary` never reached this function. With it on, every such shopper's request reached it, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each error into a failed page.
      
      The change: if there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0 {F1.1}. Nothing was spent per item this month, and `total_this_month_cents` is itself 0 {F1.2} for such an account in the fixtures. Otherwise the division is unchanged. With the flag off, nothing changes. `average_spend_per_item` and the lifetime path are untouched. They still raise for an account that has never bought anything, which the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py rely on. `render_spend_summary` and `serve_account_page` still get an int, so their return types and callers are unchanged.
      
      The tests: three new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. Two call the monthly figure directly and through `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` for a shopper with no purchases this month, and expect 0 {F1.3}. One expects 0 {F1.4} for a shopper with no history at all when the monthly flag is on. Each of these would raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. The test that expects a failure to reach the caller on the lifetime path stays as it is.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #581 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError. The error boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py then turns it into a failed account page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a setting that sent account pages through new monthly-spending code, and that code likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their pages failed.
still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Before the onset, the logs read show failures only from shoppers closing the connection. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: That code started running on account page requests when admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. From that minute, the flag's evaluations went from all off to all on. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: The feature flag an-unrelated-feature, which admin switched on at {P2.1}. The errors had already begun at the onset, before this change. Switching only monthly-spend-feature off brought the service back while an-unrelated-feature stayed on. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T20, under "What Argus did, in order"; T21, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, account pages reached a monthly spend-per-item calculation that fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The failing division would have shown up before the flag reached shoppers, and the switch would not have been made.
contributing_factors 2: The flag went from off to on for all of the service's evaluations at once. No staged rollout was seen.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing code before the error rise showed, so fewer account pages would have failed.
action_items 1: Before a feature flag can be switched on in production, require the service's tests to pass with that flag on.
action_items 2: Add test fixtures for shoppers with purchase history but no purchases in the current month, and run them on every flag-gated account page path.
action_items 3: Switch feature flags on for a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the error rate stays at its baseline.
action_items 4: Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
